statement.p: Calculate all four second-order partial derivatives and check that f_{xy}=f_{yx}. Assume the variables are restricted to a domain on which the function is defined. f(x,y) = 2\sin\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(5y\right)

static.solution: f_x = 10\cos\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(5y\right) and f_y = -10\sin\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(5y\right), so f_{xx} = -50\sin\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(5y\right), f_{yy} = -50\sin\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(5y\right), and f_{xy} = -50\cos\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(5y\right) = f_{yx} = -50\cos\mathopen{}\left(5x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(5y\right).
